subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept per-agent managed plugin installs now, and if so must this PR cover install, uninstall, update/inspect, configured-agent validation, and plugin trust semantics in one contract?
rationale: The branch changes public CLI and persisted plugin install identity for executable code, and automation cannot choose the durable product/security boundary for per-agent plugin ownership.

options.title: Require full lifecycle contract before merge
options.body: Keep this PR open but block merge until the scoped install contract covers validation, uninstall, update/inspect, trust semantics, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Narrow the PR to design discussion
options.body: Leave the canonical feature issue open and ask for a design proposal or smaller maintainer-sponsored branch before code lands.

options.title: Accept install-only scope intentionally
options.body: Maintainers could accept orphan-prone install-only behavior as an experiment, but they would own the lifecycle and security gaps called out here.

recommendation.title: Require full lifecycle contract before merge
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but block merge until the scoped install contract covers validation, uninstall, update/inspect, trust semantics, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans plugin architecture, public CLI behavior, and repository policy; steipete shows recent plugin architecture/install history and ownership-rule history.
